items.body:
## Description

Fixes #4859

`sync_pending_results` reads `self.active_runs` with a non-atomic membership check and a separate subscript:

```python
if benchmark_run_id not in self.active_runs:   # check
    return 0
run_data = self.active_runs[benchmark_run_id]   # then read
```

The worker thread deletes the entry at the end of `_sync_results_to_database` (`del self.active_runs[benchmark_run_id]`), outside `_results_sync_lock`. When that delete lands between the check and the read, the subscript raises `KeyError`. The read is before the method's `try`, so the error escapes `sync_pending_results`. `get_benchmark_results` (`benchmark_routes.py`) calls it inside a broad `try/except Exception`, so instead of the clean `0` the next poll would return, the client sees a spurious `500` on `GET /api/results/<id>`.

## Fix

Read once with `.get()`, so the presence test and the value come from the same lookup:

```python
run_data = self.active_runs.get(benchmark_run_id)
if run_data is None:
    return 0
```

A run that finished during the poll now returns `0` (nothing left to sync) rather than raising.

## Scope

For a live run the only concurrent deleter is that worker `del`; the `active_runs.pop(...)` in `start_benchmark` is a failed-start cleanup on the creating thread and cannot race a poll. The second check-then-subscript at `_sync_results_to_database:1046`/`:1049` runs on that same worker thread (the sole live-run deleter), so it cannot race the delete and is left unchanged.

## Verification

Docker (`python:3.12-slim`, `pip install -e .`) against HEAD `fc7ea75b`, with `benchmark_service.__file__` printed on both sides to confirm the mounted source was exercised:

- New test `test_returns_zero_when_entry_deleted_during_toctou_window` replaces `active_runs` with a mapping whose `__contains__` reports the key present while the entry is absent, modelling the delete firing inside the window. It fails on unmodified HEAD (`KeyError: 123`) and passes with the fix (returns `0`).
- `main` (new test, source unchanged): 1 failed, existing `TestSyncPendingResults` green. This branch: full class green; the wider `tests/benchmarks/web_api/test_benchmark_service_coverage.py` module passes.

Not exercised here: the propagation through `get_benchmark_results` to an HTTP 500 is read from the route's `try/except`, not driven end-to-end; the fix is verified at the `sync_pending_results` level.

Release note: `changelog.d/4859.bugfix.md`.

items.body:
## Problem

On the prerelease, a running benchmark logged:

```
sqlcipher3.dbapi2.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed:
    benchmark_results.benchmark_run_id, benchmark_results.query_hash
```

...in `sync_pending_results` → `session.commit()`, and the benchmark page showed **"Found 0 results"** with no progress even though tasks were completing.

## Root cause

Two code paths INSERT results from the shared `run_data["results"]` into `benchmark_results`, which has `UniqueConstraint(benchmark_run_id, query_hash)` (`uix_run_query`):

- `sync_pending_results` — runs on the **request thread** (the `/api/results/<id>` route calls it).
- `_sync_results_to_database` — runs on the **worker thread** (on completion).

The guard was a non-atomic check-then-insert keyed off `saved_indices`, with **no lock**. So two concurrent syncs — or a dataset that repeats a question (same `query_hash`) — both pass the check and insert the same row. Because it fails at `commit()`, the **entire pending batch rolls back**, so completed results never persist and the UI shows nothing.

## Fix

- Add a dedicated `_results_sync_lock` that **serializes** the two sync paths.
- Extract `_persist_unsaved_results()` — an **idempotent** insert that dedups against (a) rows already in the DB for the run, (b) the shared `saved_indices` set, and (c) duplicate `query_hash`es **within** the batch.
- Roll back the reused thread-local session on error in both paths (`safe_rollback`) so a failure can't leave a `PendingRollbackError` for the next caller.

## Tests

- New `test_benchmark_result_dedup.py` — **real SQLite** (constraint actually enforced): duplicate `query_hash` within a batch inserts once; a repeated sync with reset `saved_indices` is a no-op. Both would raise `UNIQUE constraint failed` before the fix.
- Updated the mock-based coverage tests for the new existing-hash query.
- Full `tests/benchmarks/` suite green (1436 passed).

## Note
Does not change the dual-write design (request-thread flush + worker-thread sync); it just makes both writers safe. Surfacing a clearer UI error on genuine DB-write failures (e.g. disk full) is a separate follow-up.

items.title: Benchmark monoruby alongside CRuby and push to the fork's data repo
items.body:
## Summary

Runs [monoruby](https://github.com/sisshiki1969/monoruby) in the daily benchmark loop **on the same machine as the CRuby runs**, so the monoruby results in [sisshiki1969/rubybench-data](https://github.com/sisshiki1969/rubybench-data) are directly comparable with the no-JIT/YJIT/ZJIT series (the dashboard normalizes monoruby against same-day no-JIT, which is only meaningful on identical hardware).

## Changes

- **`bin/ruby-kai1.sh`**: the results repo and commit prefix now default to `git@github.com:sisshiki1969/rubybench-data.git` and `[$(hostname)]`, both overridable via `RUBYBENCH_RESULTS_REPO` / `RUBYBENCH_RESULTS_COMMIT_PREFIX`. After the CRuby ruby-bench run, it benchmarks monoruby and syncs those results as a separate commit.
- **`benchmark/monoruby.rb`** (new): fetches and builds monoruby master (`cargo build --release`), records the actually-benchmarked revision in `results/monorubies.yml` (authoritative over the API-based `add-monoruby` workflow in rubybench-data), and runs the ruby-bench suite through `benchmark/ruby-bench/misc/monoruby-sync.rb` into `results/monoruby-bench{,-rss}/`. Idempotent per day — it exits early when today's results exist, so the systemd timer can keep re-executing it, mirroring the CRuby date tracking. Configurable via `MONORUBY_REPO` / `MONORUBY_DIR` / `MONORUBY_BENCH_TIMEOUT` / `MONORUBY_SYNC_ARGS`.
- **`bin/dashboard.rb`**: emits the `monoruby` series and `monoruby_date` / `monoruby_rss_date` into `dashboard.yml` (same logic as rubybench-data's `bin/dashboard.rb`). Also fixes two pre-existing crashes with the current benchmarks.yml: missing result files (ractor-only benchmarks) and categories not shown on the dashboard now get skipped instead of raising.
- **`bin/sync-results.rb`**: adds the `monoruby` result type ("Sync monoruby-bench results").
- **`.gitmodules`** + submodule pointer: `benchmark/ruby-bench` now tracks `sisshiki1969/ruby-bench`, which contains `harness-monoruby` and `misc/monoruby-sync.rb` (pointer includes the mkdir fix from sisshiki1969/ruby-bench#2).
- README: documents the monoruby step and the env overrides.

## Testing

- `benchmark/monoruby.rb` end-to-end with a real monoruby build (master `ab97735`): builds, records the revision in `monorubies.yml`, writes `monoruby-bench{,-rss}/*.yml` in the rubybench-data format, and a second invocation skips with "already benchmarked".
- `bin/dashboard.rb` against real rubybench-data plus a 42-benchmark monoruby sweep: with mismatched dates the monoruby column is 0.0 and `monoruby_date` is emitted separately; with aligned dates real ratios appear (25/25 micro, 15/32 other benchmarks with monoruby values).
- The CRuby/Docker path is unchanged and was not re-run here (no Docker daemon in the test environment).

## Notes for deployment

- The machine needs Docker, Ruby, a Rust toolchain (the pinned nightly is picked up from monoruby's rust-toolchain.toml), and a deploy key with push access to sisshiki1969/rubybench-data. A host Ruby ≥ 4.0 lets monoruby's stdlib probe succeed so more benchmarks can run.
- Once this machine starts pushing, stop mirroring upstream rubybench-data — the CRuby series will step to this machine's hardware, which is the intended state.

items.body:
## Summary

This PR closes all open Phase 3 issues (#8, #9, #10, #12, #13, #14) on the
`feature/p3-ml-workload-parity` branch and brings the MPI multi-driver
architecture to a fully validated state before Phase 4 Docker containerisation.

---

## Issues Closed

| Issue | Title | Status |
|---|---|---|
| #8 | Broadcast seed centroids from rank 0 before K-Means iteration loop | ✅ Fixed |
| #9 | Broadcast global mean/std from rank 0 for consistent LogReg feature standardisation | ✅ Fixed |
| #10 | Validate data integrity: MPI multi-driver vs single-driver Spark baseline | ✅ Passing |
| #12 | Benchmark sync overhead: MPI multi-driver vs single-driver baseline | ✅ Done |
| #13 | Update requirements.txt and README for mpi4py + OpenMPI (Phase 3) | ✅ Done |
| #14 | WordCount regression test: MPI multi-driver result matches baseline | ✅ Done |

---

## What Changed

### Correctness fixes (Issues #8 & #9)
- **K-Means (#8):** `allreduce.py` — rank 0 now calls `init_centroids()` on its
  local partition and `comm.Bcast` the result to all ranks before the iteration
  barrier. All ranks start iteration 1 from the **same** K centroid positions,
  making convergence reproducible across runs.
- **LogReg (#9):** `local_gradient.py` — introduced `_broadcast_global_stats()`:
  rank 0 computes global `mean` and `std` over the full dataset in a single Spark
  pass, then `comm.Bcast` both arrays to all ranks. All ranks standardise their
  features identically, matching MLlib's internal `StandardScaler` and eliminating
  the gradient-space mismatch.

### Parity validation fixes (Issue #10)
- Replaced invalid centroid L2 delta (partition-dependent) with **WCSS relative
  delta ≤ 1%** — the standard Lloyd (1982) criterion.
- Replaced invalid weight-vector L2 delta (L-BFGS vs SGD comparison) with
  **accuracy delta ≤ 3pp** on a shared 1000-row evaluation sample.
- Removed meaningless intercept delta check (MLlib real intercept vs MPI
  bias-in-weights intercept=0).
- Fixed `--metrics-dir` plumbing so metrics CSVs are actually written to
  `./metrics/` and consumed by `timing_analysis.py`.

### Instrumentation & analysis
- **`scripts/timing_analysis.py`** — timing decomposition into Spark time vs sync
  time per iteration; derives `spark_fraction`, `sync_overhead_pct`, rank
  variance, and bottleneck mode. Writes `controller_feature_matrix.csv` — the
  Objective 2b LSTM/regression input.
- **`scripts/sync_overhead_benchmark.py`** — runs single-driver baseline + reads
  MPI metrics CSVs; writes `results/sync_overhead_benchmark.csv` for Objective 2d
  evaluation (closes #12).

### Docs & dependency (Issue #13)
- `requirements.txt`: `mpi4py>=3.1` with OS-level OpenMPI note.
- `README.md`: Phase 3 Prerequisites (Ubuntu/macOS/Docker),
  `generate_datasets.py` one-time setup, all `mpirun -n 5` commands, sync
  benchmark usage, Queue deprecation note.

### Regression test (Issue #14)
- `tests/phase3/test_wordcount_mpi_vs_baseline.py` — two tests guarded with
  `@pytest.mark.skipif(mpi_size < 2)`: `test_top_n_counts_match` and
  `test_all_words_present_in_mpi_output`. A `test_skipped_in_single_rank`
  smoke-test ensures CI stays green.
- Added missing `tests/phase3/__init__.py` and `tests/logreg/__init__.py` —
  fixes `pytest tests/ -v` collection errors.

---

## Parity Results (N=5, 540 K rows)

| Metric | Value | Tolerance | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| K-Means WCSS relative delta | 0.89% | ≤ 1% | ✅ PASS |
| LogReg accuracy delta | < 2pp | ≤ 3pp | ✅ PASS |
| DATA INTEGRITY CHECK | — | — | ✅ CONFIRMED |

## Timing Analysis (N=5, 540 K rows)

| Workload | Bottleneck | Spark fraction | Sync overhead | Iterations |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| K-Means | compute | 0.963 | 3.74% | 4 (converged) |
| LogReg | sync | 0.375 | 62.51% | 14 (not converged) |

> K-Means: allocate more `cores_per_worker`.
> LogReg: tune MPI transport (UCX) or increase learning rate.

---

## Test Results

- All `tests/unit/` tests: pass without MPI
- All `tests/phase3/` MPI-guarded tests: skip cleanly in CI
- `tests/logreg/`: pass without MPI

---

## Next Phase

After this PR merges to `dev`, the next work item is **Phase 4 — Docker
containerisation**:
- One container per MPI rank, NFS-backed shared Docker volume
- OpenMPI inside containers, `mpirun` across container network
- Validate at scale on Docker Swarm (2–3 physical nodes)

Objective 2 (resource allocator) work begins in parallel on a new feature branch
once the `controller_feature_matrix.csv` dataset is expanded (vary `k`,
dataset size, `num_ranks`).

---

## Summary

Closes #3706. Three performance fixes for directory listing at scale, plus benchmarks, E2E tests, and an async bug fix.

- **N+1 `has_accessible_descendants`** → single `has_accessible_descendants_batch()` call in `_list_fast_path` (search_service.py). Loads Tiger bitmap once instead of N times per subdirectory.
- **Unbounded `metadata.list()`** → `metadata.list_iter()` streaming in `sys_readdir` (nexus_fs.py). Avoids holding two full-size lists simultaneously.
- **Per-entry `is_implicit_directory`** → pre-compute implicit dirs from sorted path list in O(N log N) for non-recursive detail listings (nexus_fs.py). Overhead ratio dropped from **166x → ~1.2x** vs `details=False` at 5K entries.

## What changed

- route dense blocked-QR matrices of at most two 32-column panels through the existing host QR implementation

After PR #142, the validated 70×35 production path measured 347.434 µs while its exact CPU final-tail arithmetic schedule measured 38.189 µs. items.title: Interim benchmark progress report + AWS result sync
items.body:
## What

One command to pull a benchmark run from the AWS box and render an **interim** progress report — safe to run while the benchmark is still going.

- **`sync-and-report.sh`** — tar the run over SSH (`--ignore-failed-read` skips the root-owned `agent/sessions` files that were aborting the archive), replace the local copy under `results/`, then render the report. Reads `REMOTE` / `REMOTE_RESULTS` from `.env`.
- **`benchmark_progress_report.py`** — from each run's `output.log` + `reward.json`, builds:
  - per-model pass / fail / pass-rate + avg task complexity
  - per-task complexity (0–10) + pass/fail
  - task × model pass matrix
  - Outputs: console tables, self-contained `report.html` (light/dark), and `deepswe_task_difficulty.csv` — all written into the run folder.
  - Reuses `aggregate.py` (`claude_stats` / `log_stats` / `task_complexity`), no new deps.

Complexity = min-max-normalized effort (steps, tool calls, output tokens, duration) pooled across all runs, scaled 0–10 — relative to the task set, not absolute.

## Config

`REMOTE` / `REMOTE_RESULTS` added to `.env.example`. Set them in your `.env` (gitignored):

```dotenv
# sync-and-report.sh — pull benchmark results from the AWS box (SSH)
REMOTE=ubuntu@ec2-XX-XX-XX-XX.compute-1.amazonaws.com
REMOTE_RESULTS=results
```

## Usage

```bash
./sync-and-report.sh                      # newest run on the remote
./sync-and-report.sh 2026-07-15__18-36-25 # a specific run
python3 benchmark_progress_report.py results/<run>   # re-render local, no pull
```

items.title: AAP-86116 Replace correlated subquery with JOIN for ansible_id annotation
items.body:
## Summary

- Adds `AssignmentResourceField` (`ForeignObject`) to `resource_registry/fields.py` that joins assignment models to `Resource` via `(content_type_id, object_id)` — both columns variable per row, no Cast needed
- Dynamically attached to `RoleUserAssignment` and `RoleTeamAssignment` via `contribute_to_class` in `ResourceRegistryConfig.ready()`, so `dab_rbac` works standalone without `resource_registry`
- Replaces `resource_ansible_id_expr()` (correlated `Subquery`) with `F('resource__ansible_id')` (JOIN-based scalar) in both service API viewsets — same annotation attribute name, zero serializer changes

## Problem

The service API annotates each assignment row with `object_ansible_id` using a correlated `Subquery` against the `Resource` table. Although the covering index makes each probe fast (~0.001ms), postgres evaluates the subquery for **every row in the scan**, including rows skipped by OFFSET pagination. This makes the full table walk (gateway sync) cost O(N²) across pages.

## Benchmark results (8K assignments)

| Scenario | Subquery (before) | F() JOIN (after) | Improvement |
|----------|-------------------|------------------|-------------|
| Page 1 (sz=50) | 0.001s | 0.002s | same |
| High offset (7970) | 0.018s | 0.003s | **6x faster** |
| Full table walk (8020 rows) | 0.258s | 0.182s | **30% faster** |

The high-offset case shows the biggest win — exactly where correlated subquery OFFSET amplification hurts most. At production scale (110K+ assignments), the O(N²) effect would be far more pronounced.

### SQL change

Before (correlated subquery, evaluated per row):
```sql
SELECT ..., (SELECT ansible_id FROM resource WHERE content_type_id = assignment.content_type_id AND object_id = assignment.object_id LIMIT 1) AS _object_ansible_id_annotation
FROM dab_rbac_roleuserassignment
```

After (LEFT JOIN, evaluated once):
```sql
SELECT ..., resource.ansible_id AS _object_ansible_id_annotation
FROM dab_rbac_roleuserassignment
LEFT OUTER JOIN dab_resource_registry_resource ON (
    assignment.object_id = resource.object_id
    AND assignment.content_type_id = resource.content_type_id
)
```

## Test plan

- [x] 294 resource_registry tests pass
- [x] No migration generated (`makemigrations --check --dry-run`)
- [ ] CI green

## Summary

Hard-path `wheel_core` is about half marking and half wrap-mul trial (DEFAULT_N on Zen 2 / 12 threads). This PR does two complementary things:

- Raise **`TILE_P_MAX` 256 → 4096** so medium primes also walk 16 KiB L1 tiles. The catalog only tried ≤512; tiling *all* primes (`p≥8192`) still loses to restart.
- Split 8-way wrap-mul into **two groups of 4** with an early exit between them. Four Newton chains fit in GPRs. Forcing a full 8-wide bitwise `|` spilled and was 2–3% *slower*.

Generator is the source of truth (`scripts/generate_wheel_core_c.py`); `wheel_core.c` is regenerated.

| Case | mean ratio (cand/orig) |
|------|-----------------------:|
| semiprime 1e9s | ~0.95–1.00 |
| M61 | ~0.96–1.00 |
| near 2^63 | ~0.94–0.97 |
| DEFAULT_N | ~0.94–0.96 (11/12 pair wins) |
| **geomean** | **~0.96** |

Order-swap geomean ~1.04 (original is slower). Default e2e suite: no regression (25% gate).

Newton-in-extract, fill-presieve per tile, two-band 64 KiB tiles, long presieve, `aligned_alloc`, extract/mark prefetch, TLS segment buffers, `orb` asm (GCC already emits it), forced 8-wide `|`, TILE_P_MAX ≥ 8192.

items.body:
## Symptom

The landing page (js2.loopdive.com) showed a **stale and inflated** test262 number — **32,788** (from 07:44Z) — while the honest current number is **32,165**. Not just stale: 32,788 predates today's assert_throws harness tightening (#3104/#3285), so the public page advertised a figure ~600 too high for hours, while every pipeline layer reported success.

## Root cause

`baseline-summary-sync.yml` (#1951, hourly) syncs the `loopdive/js2wasm-baselines` repo → `public/benchmarks/results/test262-report.json` (which `deploy-pages` publishes). Its drift check is inconsistent:

- **Standalone** check compares against the **public** file it overwrites ✓
- **Host** check compares against the **in-repo** `benchmarks/results/test262-current.json` ✗

The commit step copies the report into `public/…test262-report.json`, but that file was a copy *target* and never the host comparison *baseline*.

Failure sequence: a FORCED baseline refresh updated the baselines repo **and** the in-repo copy in lockstep to 32,165 → host check sees `baselines == in-repo` → `HOST_UNCHANGED=1` → standalone also unchanged → "nothing to sync" → job exits **before** the copy → `public/` freezes at 32,788 permanently. The `force` input doesn't help (it only bypasses the queue guard, checked *after* the skip).

This is a **change-detection correctness bug**, not a transient — the in-repo/baselines lockstep makes it permanent until they diverge again.

## Fix

One line: host drift check compares against `public/benchmarks/results/test262-report.json`, mirroring the standalone check. Plus a comment recording the trap.

After merge, the next sync detects the real public-vs-baselines drift (32,788 ≠ 32,165), copies, and `deploy-pages` republishes → landing page shows 32,165. I'll dispatch one sync post-merge to correct the page immediately rather than wait for the delayed cron.

items.title: Build AgentFS and Turso knowledge base POC
items.body:
## Summary

Builds the disposable AgentFS + Turso Sync knowledge-base proof of concept and records the evidence needed to decide whether the proposed architecture should continue.

The prototype includes:

- a Bun/TypeScript daemon and thin local CLI
- AgentFS-compatible inode/chunk storage backed by the current Turso Sync driver
- transactional Markdown reads, writes, moves, deletes, and plain-file export
- HTTP API, two-device sync/conflict scenarios, AgentFS interoperability probe, and performance benchmarks
- committed raw results and a detailed recommendation in `POC.md`

## Result and impact

The POC disproves the architecture as originally proposed:

- disconnected replicas can allocate colliding AgentFS autoincrement inode/dentry IDs, causing one independently created file to disappear on convergence
- the official AgentFS CLI/mount cannot open the database while the daemon owns it
- same-document edits converge by last-push-wins and silently lose the earlier body

Turso Sync itself handled BLOBs, outages, restarts, renames, and deletes correctly, and Bun performance was strong. The recommendation is to keep Bun/TypeScript and Turso for the next experiment, replace the synchronized AgentFS schema with UUID/text identities plus explicit conflict preservation, and prototype an embedded filesystem adapter.

## Validation

- `bun test`: 3 passed, 0 failed
- `bun run typecheck`: passed
- remote comparison: one commit ahead of `main`, 21 intended files, no dependency directories
- the committed sync scenario intentionally records a failing architectural assertion because it reproduces the file-loss defect

S1 of the observability sprint persists those runs and turns them into alerts. It adds no new measurement — every number here is one the caller already had.

- api/cron/daily-ml.js: record the benchmark sweep result.
- healthBundle.js: expose settlementHealth / benchmarkHealth, read in the existing Promise.all (KV only, no SQL, no upstream calls, so the bundle's cost is unchanged).

- settlement_pending — finished fixtures with an ungraded recommended pick. medium at >= SETTLEMENT_PENDING_WARN (5), high at >= _CRITICAL (20).

items.title: Scale Take across cores with a sync.Map bucket store
items.body:
Makes `Take` scale across cores by removing the global lock from the read path. This is measured, not guessed: I profiled the hot path, found the bottleneck, fixed it, and re-benchmarked.

## What the profile showed

Under parallel load, 78% of CPU was in `sync/atomic.(*Int32).Add`. Every `Take` took the store's `RWMutex` read lock, and each `RLock`/`RUnlock` mutates one shared `readerCount` counter. A read lock isn't free concurrency: all cores contend on that single cache line, so throughput collapses as cores go up.

## The fix

Buckets are created once (a key's first `Take`) and then read on every subsequent `Take`. That is exactly `sync.Map`'s read-mostly case: existing-key loads hit its read-only snapshot with no writes to shared state, so there's no cache-line bouncing. Swapped `map[string]*bucket` + `RWMutex` for a `sync.Map`.

## Results

Hot-path micro-benchmarks (`memorystore/bench_test.go`, Apple M4 Pro, 14 threads):

| benchmark | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `Take_parallel_manyKeys` (many clients) | ~90 ns/op | ~14-45 ns/op |
| `Take_parallel_hotKey` (one hot key) | ~140 ns/op | ~124 ns/op |
| `Take_serial` | ~43 ns/op | ~40 ns/op |

The many-keys path (the realistic high-concurrency case) is the headline: it drops from ~90ns to as low as ~14ns. It's noisy at that speed, but it's always a large win and statistically significant (p=0.000, n=12). Zero allocations on the `Take` path, unchanged.

Against the other libraries (comparison suite, memory backend, lower is faster):

| | serial | parallel |
|---|---|---|
| **go-limiter** | **60.6 ns** | **19.2 ns** |
| ulule | 139 ns | 32 ns |
| throttled | 91 ns | 412 ns |
| tollbooth | 150 ns | 250 ns |

go-limiter is the fastest per-key limiter in both, and fastest overall in the concurrent case. (`go.uber.org/ratelimit` is faster serial, but it's a single global blocking limiter with no per-key lookup, so it's a different tool.)

## Also here

- Fixed a bug in the comparison harness: `init` built a local slice but never populated the package-level `sessions` map, so every benchmark hammered a single empty-string key instead of 1000 distinct sessions. The parallel numbers above are only meaningful with that fixed.
- `Config.InitialAlloc` is now a no-op (kept for compatibility). `sync.Map` has no pre-sizing.

Correctness holds under `-race`. I also tried swapping the per-bucket `RWMutex` for a `Mutex`; it helped the uncontended path ~6% but regressed the hot-single-key path ~15%, so I dropped it.

items.title: fix(#3379): baseline-sync staleness guard must measure public/, not the in-repo copy (follow-up to #3375)
items.body:
Follow-up to #3375. That fix made the host drift-check correctly **detect** public staleness (`host_unchanged=0`), but the sync still didn't update `public/` — a second instance of the same "measures the in-repo copy, not public/" bug.

## Root cause

After drift is detected, a churn guard skips the sync if the merge queue is busy **and** the committed summary is `< 6h` old. The age was computed from the **in-repo** `benchmarks/results/test262-current.json`, which forced promotes refresh in lockstep with the baselines repo — so it reads ~0h even when `public/benchmarks/results/test262-report.json` (the file the landing page serves) is hours stale.

Observed after #3375 landed (sync run 29604427308):
```
Drift detected (host_unchanged=0 standalone_unchanged=0); queue=15 committed-summary age=0h force=false
Merge queue busy and summary <6h old — skipping this cycle.
```
`host_unchanged=0` (the #3375 fix working) but `age=0h` from the wrong file + `queue=15` → skip. During active dev the in-repo file keeps getting refreshed, so `age` never crosses 6h and a busy queue skips the sync **indefinitely** — the page only self-heals via a manual `force=true`.

## Fix

Measure the age of `public/benchmarks/results/test262-report.json`. With #3375 + this, the sync both **detects** public drift and **acts** on a stale public file — no manual force needed.

(The page was already force-corrected to 32,165 for now; this makes it self-heal going forward.)

| Storage | Write ms | Rows/s | Filter ms | Group ms | Scan ms | Disk KB |

| VARCHAR col | 80 | 1,250,000 | 38 | 48 | 36 | 3,084 |

- Read speedup: **2.1x** filter, **2.6x** group by, **1.6x** scan vs JSON
- Disk: **1.8-2.0x** smaller

### RawDuck vs Opaque Storage: 500k rows

| Storage | Write ms | Rows/s | Filter ms | Group ms | Scan ms | Disk KB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| RawDuck | 193 | 2,590,674 | 16 | 17 | 14 | 4,876 |
| JSON col | 258 | 1,937,984 | 39 | 59 | 34 | 13,580 |

At 100k rows, RawDuck pays ~25-33% write overhead for shredding but reads 1.6-2.6x faster and uses 2x less disk. At 500k+ rows, columnar compression amortizes the shredding cost entirely — RawDuck writes **25% faster** than opaque storage while reading 2.4-3.5x faster and using 2.8x less disk.

items.body:
<!-- What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes here. -->

This PR targets certain parts of the PET forward pass. The list of changes and the overall gain in speed is listed below. 

## Summary

Reduces PET inference latency by 7-10% (wall time) and up to 23% (steady-state throughput) by cutting CPU kernel launches and eliminating GPU-CPU host synchronizations in the `systems_to_batch` preprocessing pipeline.

The model is launch-bound on GPU (H100): most time is spent in CPU-side dispatch, not GPU compute. These changes target `src/metatrain/pet/modules/` (`nef.py`, `structures.py`) and propagate the updated function signatures to FlashMD.

## Changes

### `structures.py` — `concatenate_structures`
Replaced per-system `torch.full` / `torch.arange` / offset-add in a Python loop with a single `repeat_interleave(output_size=...)` call that offsets all edges and builds system/atom indices in batch. The `output_size` parameter is critical — without it, `repeat_interleave` does a host sync to read the sum of repeats off the GPU.

### `structures.py` — adaptive cutoff masking
Six separate boolean-indexing operations (`x[bool_mask]`), each internally running its own `aten::nonzero` kernel, replaced with a single `torch.nonzero(...).squeeze(-1)` followed by six `index_select` calls that reuse the precomputed index.

### `nef.py` — `get_nef_indices`
- Accepts pre-computed `num_neighbors` tensor (from the caller's `bincount`) instead of re-running `bincount` internally.
- Replaced boolean-mask scatter (`nef_indices[nef_mask] = argsort`) with flat-index scatter via `cumsum` + direct index computation, eliminating a hidden `nonzero` kernel.

### `nef.py` — `get_corresponding_edges`
- Accepts `(centers, neighbors, cell_shifts)` as separate arguments, removing a `torch.concatenate` at the call site.
- Vectorized 6 separate `.min()` / `.max()` reduction kernels into 2 calls to `.amin(dim=0)` / `.amax(dim=0)`.

### `nef.py` — `compute_reversed_neighbor_list`
Accepts `nef_to_edges_neighbor` (already computed by `get_nef_indices`) as a direct edge-to-position lookup, replacing the previous approach that built a full-size lookup table via boolean-mask gather/scatter and a `.max().item()` host sync.

### `structures.py` — host sync elimination
Replaced `int(torch.sum(~nef_mask))` (GPU-to-CPU sync every forward pass) with `reverse_neighbor_index.numel() - centers.shape[0]` (pure shape arithmetic).

### FlashMD
Updated `experimental/flashmd/modules/structures.py` to match the new function signatures and applied the same host sync fix.

## Benchmark results

Benchmarked on H100 with `pet-mad-xs-v1.5.0` checkpoint, 20 warmup + 100 timed iterations.

### Per-iteration wall time (with per-iteration `cuda.synchronize`)

| Preset | Atoms | Systems | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c8 | 8 | 1 | 9.07 | 8.37 | **-7.7%** |
| c216 | 216 | 1 | 12.64 | 11.78 | **-6.8%** |
| cu-batch-32 | 128 | 32 | 46.47 | 41.86 | **-9.9%** |

### Steady-state throughput (single sync at end)

| Preset | main (ms/iter) | this PR (ms/iter) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| c8 | 9.07 | 8.34 | **-8.1%** |
| c216 | 15.24 | 11.75 | **-22.9%** |
| cu-batch-32 | 45.50 | 40.74 | **-10.5%** |

The throughput improvement on c216 (23%) is larger than the latency improvement (7%) because the eliminated host syncs were breaking GPU pipelining across iterations: mid-iteration `.item()` calls and implicit syncs from boolean indexing forced the CPU to wait for prior GPU work, preventing overlap between consecutive iterations.

### Per-stage breakdown (profiled iteration, CPU time)

| Stage | c8 | c216 | cu-batch-32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `systems_to_batch` | -14.2% | -10.4% | **-42.0%** |
| `adaptive_cutoff_masking` | **-51.5%** | -15.1% | **-52.6%** |
| `_calculate_features` | -5.2% | -1.7% | -2.1% |
| `post-processing` | -2.9% | -4.1% | +0.3% |

items.body:
Resolves #773

## Summary

Add support for S3 aws-chunked streaming uploads (`STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD`, `STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD-TRAILER`, `STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER`, and `Content-Encoding: aws-chunked` under `UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD`) to the S3 gateway. The aws-chunked body is de-framed at the transport boundary so stored blobs, dedup, CRUSH placement, `getFile` hash verification, and splay/chain replication all use the *decoded* payload and its real content hash.

## What changed

- **`src/transport/aws_chunked.go`** (new): `awsChunkedReader` decodes the aws-chunked wire grammar (`<hex-size>[;chunk-signature=<64hex>]\r\n<raw data>\r\n` … terminating `0[;...]\r\n\r\n` + optional trailer block) with strict bounds — header lines ≤ 1 KiB, per-chunk size ≤ AWS 8 MiB cap, total decoded bytes capped at `common.MaxFileSize`. Computes the decoded SHA-256 and byte count on the stream.
- **Signed per-chunk verification**: each chunk is verified against the chained SigV4 streaming string-to-sign (`AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD\n<date>\n<scope>\n<prevSig>\n<emptySHA256>\n<hex(sha256(chunkData))>`) keyed by `deriveSigningKey` and seeded with the request signature. Reproduces the AWS documentation vector exactly (chunk sigs `ad80c7…`, `005562…`, `b6c6ea…`). The canonical header signature check keeps using the `STREAMING-*` literal as the payload hash, per the AWS spec.
- **`src/transport/s3_communicator.go`**: `HandshakeServer` detects streaming PUTs, derives the signing context from the verified request, emits `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` for `Expect: 100-continue`, sets a size-based read deadline, spills de-framed bytes to a bounded temp file, resolves `m.meta.Hash`/`m.meta.Size` to the decoded values (cross-checked against `X-Amz-Decoded-Content-Length`), and replays the spill through `S3Communicator.Read()`. Spill is closed/removed on every exit path. `ReceiveMetadata` (OPTIONS-handshake path) rejects `STREAMING-*` since it cannot authenticate chunk signatures.
- **Error mapping**: chunk signature mismatch → `403 SignatureDoesNotMatch`; malformed framing / decoded-length mismatch → `400 InvalidArgument`; oversized → `413 EntityTooLarge`.
- **Docs**: `docs/PROTOCOL.md` documents the streaming variants, de-framing, chunk signature algorithm, and the unsigned-streaming security posture.
- **Spec**: `openspec/changes/aws-chunked-streaming/` (proposal + spec + tasks).

## Test plan

- Unit tests reproduce the AWS documentation vector; corrupted signature, truncated chunk, missing terminator, unsigned trailer, oversized chunk, oversize total, header-line overflow.
- Gateway e2e: signed streaming PUT stores de-framed content with resolved `meta.Hash`/`meta.Size`; corrupted chunk signature → `EACCES`; `Expect: 100-continue`; decoded-length mismatch → `EBADMSG`; oversized → `413`; `STREAMING-*` on the handshake path rejected.
- Benchmarks: `BenchmarkAWSChunkedReaderSigned` (~89 MB/s) and `BenchmarkAWSChunkedReaderUnsigned` (~97 MB/s); results synced to `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` / `.github/data/benchmark_history.csv` by the pre-commit hook.
- `go vet`, `gofmt`, and all per-module test suites pass (`src` root, `common`, `transport`, `client`, `server`, `storage`, `metrics`, `crypto`, `p2p`).

## Changelog

- Added: aws-chunked streaming PUT support (signed and unsigned variants)
- Added: per-chunk SigV4 signature verification
- Added: `Expect: 100-continue` handling and size-based read deadlines for streaming bodies
- Added: spec `openspec/changes/aws-chunked-streaming/`
- Docs: `docs/PROTOCOL.md` S3 streaming section
